title: Finding a file called Untitled?
hook: “Untitled” can contain the exact detail you remember.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that a search can look inside documents, so a file titled 'Untitled' can be found by a word in its text

misconception: Searching for a document means searching its title.
objective: Distinguish title-only search from content search.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: “Untitled” can contain the exact detail you remember. Which finds the document containing “telescope”? Correct option: Body search. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.

claims.text: The body contains the remembered term while the title does not. Expanding the searched field changes which documents can match.
claims.source: Derivation from the explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and transformations in src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts; app documentation below provides command/filter context, not evidence of productivity gains or of every fixture-specific choice. Google Drive Help, Search for files in Google Drive, filtering and advanced search; retrieved 2026-10-13: https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2375114?hl=en . Exercise fixtures do not reproduce every Drive search behaviour. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Read StudyLesson.tsx FileStage and studyModels.ts fileResult first. Fixture: item name 'untitled', body 'telescope notes'. Step 1 (Titles only) filters r.name.includes('telescope'): 0 matches. Step 2 (Search bodies) filters r.value: 1 match, 'untitled'. So the body holds the term and the title does not, and switching the searched field changes the matches (0 to 1). Derivation from the fixture; the Google Drive Help page (not opened) is context only and not relied on.

claims.note: FC pass 50 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): RE-CHECKED, STAYS VERIFIED (W-1084). The r11 learner review (2026-10-15-learner-adult-beginner-r11.md, point 27) and the board item read 'The number is in the body' as a stage claim and called it false because the stage word is 'telescope'. It is not a stage claim. It is meta.recall.why, the explanation for the recall card, whose question reads: 'You remember a document mentions 'invoice 4471' but not its title. Which search can find it?' (keyed: 'Search file contents for 4471'). 'The number' is 4471. It is in the body by stipulation, and a title-only search does not read the body, so the sentence is true where the learner meets it. It also matches recall-patch-study.lines.txt line 49. The real problem is presentation: the trust sheet (src/lib/trust.ts, DemoCard) lists the sentence without the recall question, so out of context it seems to point at the stage. Suggested fix for demo-builder (claim text, not a correction): make it self-contained, e.g. 'In the recall card, the invoice number 4471 is in the file's body; a title-only search never looks there.' If the text changes, reset to unverified for a re-check.

recall.question: You remember a document mentions 'invoice 4471' but not its title. Which search can find it?
options: Sort all titles from A to Z
recall.why: The number is in the body; a title-only search never looks there.
